content.title: No. 1 Arizona books first Final Four appearance in 25 years with 79-64 Elite 8 win over No. 2 Purdue
content.text: Arizona is heading to the Final Four for the first time since 2001.The No. 1 Wildcats used a second-half blitz to put away No. 2 Purdue 79-64 and win its first Elite Eight game in six tries since making the national title game 25 years ago.AdvertisementArizona took over midway through the second half after Purdue led by seven at halftime. The Wildcats had the game tied less than five minutes into the second half and started pulling away after that.After tying the game at 42-42, Arizona outscored the Boilermakers 24-11 to build a 13-point lead with six minutes to go. The flurry came as Purdue went ice cold from the field and Big 12 player of the year Jaden Bradley was making shots like this.Overall, Arizona outscored Purdue 48-26 in the second half. Star freshman forward Koa Peat had 20 points, while Ivan Kharchenkov scored 18 as he also took on the task of guarding Purdue’s Braden Smith.AdvertisementThe win is the 13th straight for the Wildcats as they won the Big 12 regular season and tournament titles. They’ll play the winner of Sunday’s Elite Eight game between No. 1 Michigan and No. 6 Tennessee in the Final Four.Arizona is finally back in the Final FourThere’s no program with more deep tournament runs without a Final Four since the Wildcats last got there under coach Lute Olson.“Personally I feel good, I’m most happy for these Arizona fans. You guys deserve this,” Lloyd said in his postgame interview on TBS before taking the microphone from sideline reporter Allie LaForce to address the Arizona fans in attendance.Advertisement“There’s a good-looking guy with white hair looking down on us who’s happy,” Lloyd said about Olson.Olson, who died at the age of 85 in 2020, coached the Wildcats from 1983 to 2008 and led Arizona to the 1997 national title.Before Saturday night, Arizona had made 12 Sweet 16 appearances and made the Elite Eight five times since that last Final Four appearance. But every single one of those tournament runs ended before the third weekend of the NCAA tournament.And even getting to the Elite Eight became a tough task in recent years.Until a win over Arkansas on Thursday night, Arizona had lost four straight Sweet 16 games since making the Elite Eight in 2015. Three of those four losses also came as either a No. 1 or No. 2 seed.AdvertisementThere was no stopping this Wildcats team, however. Especially with the way it took care of the ball in the second half. After turning it over six times in the first 20 minutes, Arizona didn’t commit a single turnover in the second half.Purdue’s Trey Kaufman-Renn limited to 23 minutesAfter tipping in the game-winner against Texas on Thursday night in the Sweet 16, Trey Kaufman-Renn spent a lot of time on the bench against Arizona.Kaufman-Renn picked up his second foul just seconds after re-entering the game with over 12 minutes to go in the first half. Purdue coach Matt Painter didn’t keep Kaufman-Renn out the rest of the half — he returned for short shifts after spending a couple minutes on the bench — but the star forward played just nine minutes before halftime.AdvertisementHe then made it less than a minute into the second half before picking up his third foul. That sent Kaufman-Renn to the bench again, though he only picked up one foul the rest of the way and finished with 10 points.His absence forced Purdue to play Daniel Jacobsen 13 minutes after he had played 14 minutes over Purdue’s previous three games of the NCAA tournament. The 7-foot-2 sophomore missed his only field goal attempt and both his free throws while recording a block.Smith, who set the Division I career record for assists in the first round of the tournament, finished his college career with 13 points and seven assists against the Wildcats. Smith played all but five minutes despite suffering a brief injury scare in the second half when he rolled his right ankle while playing defense. After spending a moment on the ground, Smith retied his shoe and stayed in the game.
